content.text:
Resubmitted with the IP limb repaired in operative language.

**What changed in response to the verifier:**

1. **Limb (d) rewritten to express infringement-claim language** — it now reads "*any allegation that the RevMed Licensed Technology, or Sanofi's exercise of the licenses granted to it under this Agreement, infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right of a Third Party*", i.e. an explicit allegation-of-infringement trigger rather than a causal "the infringement ... by" formulation. That is the contract's analogue of "Services or Deliverables infringe", since this collaborative research/licence agreement has no Services or Deliverables construct.
2. **Defined term confirmed** — "RevMed Licensed Technology" is defined at Section 1.99 ("RevMed Background Technology, RevMed Sole Program Technology and RevMed's undivided one-half ownership ... of the Joint Program Technology"), so limb (d) contains no undefined term; p0124 is now cited in the finding.
3. **14.2 housekeeping checked** — limbs (a) and (b) remain the only operative items and read correctly as "(a) ... ; or (b) ...", with (c)/(d) marked "[Intentionally omitted.]" so the retained flush "except in each case ((a) through (d))" carve-out in p0591 is not a dangling reference; no other provision cross-refers to 14.2(c)–(d).
4. **Deliberate non-changes** — we did not add a separate "breach of Applicable Law" limb (already reached by 14.1(c) with the Section 13.4(b) compliance covenant, mapped as already met), and we did not add a "notwithstanding Section 10.7" override, which would be a broad override where none is needed. The commercial pushback risk on narrowing 14.2 is flagged in the comment/rationale for the negotiator.
